title: Hot Cocoa Holiday Cupcakes
shortDescription: Rich chocolate cupcakes with marshmallow swirl frosting, ready in about 43 minutes total with 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes taste like a mug of hot cocoa in cake form. The base is a deep chocolate cupcake with a touch of cinnamon and espresso powder to boost the cocoa flavor. On top goes a fluffy marshmallow swirl frosting that melts a little like a topping on cocoa. I tested this recipe in my home kitchen on a snowy afternoon while my kids waited by the oven. The marshmallow frosting sets up soft, so pipe it right before serving for the best swirl. A sprinkle of mini marshmallows and cocoa powder on top makes these look like they came straight from a holiday cocoa bar. They are simple enough for a weeknight bake but special enough for a cookie exchange or class party.
ingredients: Mini marshmallows and cocoa powder, for topping
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk the flour, cocoa powder, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, and espresso powder in a bowl.
Beat the butter and sugar together until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add the eggs one at a time, then mix in the vanilla extract.
Add the dry ingredients in two batches, alternating with the buttermilk. Mix just until combined.
Stir in the hot water last. The batter will be thin, and that is normal.
Divide the batter among the liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely before frosting.
For the frosting, whisk egg whites, sugar, and cream of tartar over a double boiler until sugar dissolves.
Remove from heat and beat with a mixer on high speed for 5 to 7 minutes, until thick and glossy. Add vanilla.
Pipe the marshmallow frosting onto cooled cupcakes right away, using a large open star tip.
Top with mini marshmallows and a light dusting of cocoa powder before serving.
tips: Make the marshmallow frosting last. It softens fast, so pipe it right before you serve the cupcakes.
Use a kitchen torch for a few seconds on the frosting to get a toasted marshmallow look.
Room temperature eggs mix in smoother and give a more even cake crumb.
If you do not have a double boiler, a heatproof bowl set over a pot of simmering water works fine.

faq.question: Why is my marshmallow frosting runny instead of fluffy?
faq.answer: The sugar syrup was likely too warm when you started beating it. Let the bowl cool for a minute off the heat before you whip it on high speed.

faq.question: Can I make the marshmallow frosting ahead of time?
faq.answer: This frosting is best made the same day. It loses its fluffy texture and starts to weep if it sits too long before piping.

faq.question: What does the espresso powder do in the cake?
faq.answer: Espresso powder deepens the chocolate flavor without adding a coffee taste. You can skip it, but the cocoa flavor will be milder.

faq.question: Can I use marshmallow fluff instead of making frosting from scratch?
faq.answer: Yes, folding marshmallow fluff into whipped butter is a faster shortcut. It will taste sweeter and hold its shape a bit longer than the classic swirl.

conclusion: These Hot Cocoa Holiday Cupcakes bring the cozy feel of a winter mug straight to your dessert table. Bake a batch for your next holiday gathering and watch them disappear fast.
